The University of Liverpool's Cat Prospective Aging and Welfare Study (CatPAWS), which follows a group of pet cats from middle age into later life, is celebrating more than nine years of work to improve the health and welfare of cats more than 7 years old.

Part of the Feline Healthy Aging Clinic, sponsored by Royal Canin, the study recruited its first cat in February 2017. Over the last nine years, 243 cats have been recruited. The oldest is Pou Pou, who is now more than 18 years old.

# Cornell launches clinical trial of once-weekly GLP-1 therapy for feline weight management

Author(s)Bob Alaburda, Associate Editorial Director

Fact checked by: Kelly King

Cornell University is enrolling client-owned cats in an 11-week trial of AKS-562c, a once-weekly GLP-1 Fc-fusion candidate designed to reduce appetite and produce clinically meaningful weight loss while closely monitoring safety and tolerability.

A Cornell University–led clinical trial is enrolling client-owned cats to evaluate AKS-562c, a once-weekly GLP-1 Fc-fusion candidate developed by Akston, for safety and efficacy as an adjunct to nutritional management of excess body condition. Pending trial results, the therapy could become a practical pharmacologic adjunct to multimodal weight-management plans in feline patients.¹

# Cancer Treatment for Cats and Dogs

A cancer diagnosis for your pet can be devastating as a pet owner. Much like humans, cats and dogs can develop various forms of cancer that require expert treatment. At Southfields Veterinary Specialists, we understand this difficult time and are here to help ensure that your pets get the best levels of care and treatment post diagnosis, and every chance at being able to enjoy a happy life.

 

Our dedicated team of veterinary oncology staff are committed to providing the best cancer treatments for cats and dogs, ensuring that both you and your pet is fully supported in their journey. We treat each cat or dog with the respect that they deserve and tailor cancer treatments to their needs.

 

 

If you have noticed a change in your cat or dogs’ behaviours or habits, speak to your local veterinary practice immediately and seek a referral to Southfields Veterinary Specialists. We can confirm a cancer diagnosis early and provide effective, tailored cancer treatments for cats and dogs.

 

## Comprehensive Cancer Treatments for Cats and Dogs

At Southfields Veterinary Specialists, we provide a range of cancer treatments for cats and dogs that are tailored to meet their individual needs. We have a team of highly skilled veterinary oncologists, surgeons and nurses that work closely together to create a personalised treatment plan for your pet, targeting optimal health as a result.

 

### Why choose Southfields Veterinary Specialists for Cancer Treatments for Cats and Dogs?

When your pet faces a cancer diagnosis, it’s important to have a compassionate and experienced team supporting you and your pets along their journey. At Southfields Veterinary Specialists, we offer the highest levels of treatments and services for small animals. For those in need of cancer treatments for cats and dogs, coming to Southfields Veterinary Specialists offers:

  * Advanced diagnostic tools: Accurate diagnosis is the foundation for successful cancer treatment for cats and dogs. Our state-of-the-art diagnostic facilities ensures that we can give the correct diagnosis with effective treatments that target the best chance at recovery for your pet.
  * A collaborative approach to care: We work as an in-house, multidisciplinary team alongside your primary care vets to ensure that your pet gets a collaborative approach to their cancer treatment.

##### This study aims to determine if a new experimental drug for dogs diagnosed with glioma, a type of brain tumor, is safe and feasible for brain tumor patients.

The experimental drug works by blocking a process that cancer cells use to protect themselves and survive. By stopping this process while dogs are also receiving radiation therapy, we hope to improve how well the tumor responds to treatment.
